cards.prose: Matthew has the two disciples sent from *the mount of Olives* before anything else happens on this ride. Zechariah says that in the day Yahuah (the LORD) goes out against the nations gathered at Jerusalem, his feet stand on that same mountain. Yahusha (Jesus) begins his entry into the city from the ground the prophet marked for that day.
cards.member_phrase: his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east
cards.member_sentence: The feet of Yahuah (the LORD) stand on this mountain in the day he goes out against the nations gathered at Jerusalem.

cards.prose: Saul went looking for his father's lost asses and, finding nothing, was told of a man of Elohim (God) in the city who could show them the way. In Matthew the asses are not lost. Yahusha (Jesus) says where they are, and two disciples have only to loose them and bring them to him.
cards.member_phrase: lest my father leave caring for the asses, and take thought for us
cards.member_sentence: Saul's search for his father's lost asses brings him to the land of Zuph, where he is sent to a man of Elohim (God) to learn his way.
cards.flag: The pair is thin; the old note only named Saul and the asses, so I wrote what the verses show and left out the anointing since that text was not given.

cards.prose: Matthew says the entry came about *that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet*. Isaiah has the same message for the same woman: Yahuah (the LORD) has sent word to the end of the world to tell the daughter of Zion that her salvation comes, and that his reward and his work are with him.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sends word to the end of the world that the daughter of Zion's salvation is coming, with his reward and his work with him.

cards.prose: Zephaniah tells the daughter of Zion to sing and shout, and gives the reason a few lines on: *the king of Yashar'el (Israel), even Yahuah (LORD), is in the midst of thee* (Zephaniah 3:15). In Matthew the word to the daughter of Zion is the same call to be glad, and the cause is the same, someone near who is coming to her.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The daughter of Zion is told to sing and shout, with the reason given in the lines that follow: Yahuah (the LORD) is in her midst.

cards.prose: *Save now* is what the crowd's cry of *Hosanna* means, and it is the psalm's own prayer. The pilgrims sang it at the feast, and here it is sung over a man riding into Jerusalem, with the very next line of the psalm in their mouths too, the blessing on the one who comes in the name of Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Save now is the plea behind the word Hosanna, the prayer the pilgrims sang at the feast.

cards.prose: When the crowd cries *Hosanna to the Son of David*, this is the promise behind the name. Yahuah (the LORD) told David that a seed of his would come after him and that he would establish that seed's kingdom. The crowd is not flattering Yahusha (Jesus). It is naming him as the one the promise was made about.
cards.member_phrase: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises David a seed who will come out of his own body and whose kingdom he will establish.

cards.prose: Isaiah gives the line the crowd's *Son of David* comes from. David's father was Jesse, and out of the stem of Jesse a rod comes forth with a Branch growing from his roots. The chapter goes on to say how he judges: *with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth* (Isaiah 11:4).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: A rod comes out of the stem of Jesse and a Branch from his roots, the line the crowd names when it says Son of David.

cards.prose: *Son of David* also rings with Isaiah's root of Jesse standing as an ensign of the people. The prophet says what the ensign is for in the verses after it: he *shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth* (Isaiah 11:12). The crowd is shouting at the one who raises the signal for the scattered to come home.
cards.member_phrase: there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek
cards.member_sentence: The root of Jesse stands as an ensign for the people, the signal by which the scattered are called home.

cards.prose: Jeremiah's righteous Branch raised to David is the same son of David the crowd names, one who reigns and does judgment and justice. The verses around it say who he is raised for: *I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them* (Jeremiah 23:3), with Yahudah (Judah) saved and Yashar'el (Israel) dwelling safely in his days.
cards.member_phrase: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to raise up a righteous Branch for David, who will reign and execute judgment and justice.

cards.prose: Ezekiel promises one shepherd over the flock, *my servant David*, and the lines before it say why the flock needs one: the diseased had been pushed with horns *till ye have scattered them abroad* (Ezekiel 34:21). The crowd shouting to David's son is shouting to the shepherd of a scattered flock.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sets one shepherd, his servant David, over the flock that had been scattered.

cards.prose: Ezekiel's David is king over them, and *they all shall have one shepherd*. The verse says what that people does: they walk in his judgments and keep his statutes. The verses before it say who they are, that *they shall be no more two nations* (Ezekiel 37:22). The Son of David the crowd hails is king over both houses together, and over a people that keeps the commandments.
cards.member_phrase: they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them
cards.member_sentence: David is king over the whole restored people, one shepherd for all of them, and they walk in his judgments and keep his statutes.

cards.prose: Matthew shows Yahusha (Jesus) going straight into the temple and driving out the sellers. Malachi says Yahuah (the Lord), whom they seek, will *suddenly come to his temple*, and the lines after it say what he does on arrival: he sits as a refiner and *shall purify the sons of Levi* (Malachi 3:3), so that they may offer an offering in righteousness. The cleansing is the refining begun at the house.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (Lord), whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the Lord), whom they seek, comes suddenly to his temple, and the verses after it say he comes to purify.

cards.prose: Zechariah's last verse says that in that day there shall be *no more the Canaanite* in the house, and the word he uses means a trader. Matthew has the house full of those who sold and bought, and Yahusha (Jesus) overturning their tables. What the prophet gave as the sign of the holy day, he begins with his own hands.
cards.member_phrase: in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)
cards.member_sentence: On the day every pot in Jerusalem is holy, no trader stands any more in the house.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the house of prayer, and Isaiah says in the next breath who it is for: *which gathereth the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel) saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him* (Isaiah 56:8). So *all people* there are the gathered, the outcasts brought home and the others gathered beside them, and the house names no one else being added. The sellers had filled it with stalls.
cards.member_phrase: for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people
cards.member_sentence: The house of prayer for all people is the house Yahuah (the LORD) fills with the outcasts he gathers, and the verse after it names them.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the charge, and the chapter it comes from shows what the charge was. The prophet asks if they will steal, murder, commit adultery and swear falsely, and then stand in the house and say *We are delivered to do all these abominations* (Jeremiah 7:10). They kept repeating *The temple of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 7:4), and trusted the building while they broke the commandments.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The house called by his name had become a den of robbers in the eyes of the people who trusted it while breaking the commandments.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) quotes one line out of Jeremiah 7, and this is where the whole word begins. It was spoken standing in the gate of the house to all of Yahudah (Judah) coming in to worship, and it opens with a call to *Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place* (Jeremiah 7:3), and a warning not to trust *The temple of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 7:4), said three times over.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The whole word against the house begins here, spoken in the gate of the house to everyone of Yahudah (Judah) coming in to worship.

cards.prose: The blind and the lame come to him in the temple and are healed, and Isaiah lists that among the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes. The chapter says it plainly: *he will come and save you* (Isaiah 35:4), with the eyes of the blind opened and, a few lines on, *the lame man leap as an hart* (Isaiah 35:6).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: When Elohim (God) comes to save, the eyes of the blind are opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.

cards.prose: The words *The blind and the lame shall not come into the house* come out of David's taking of Zion, where the Jebusites had boasted *Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither* (2 Samuel 5:6). It was a saying from a siege. Matthew has the blind and the lame coming to Yahusha (Jesus) inside the temple itself, and he heals them there.
cards.member_phrase: The blind and the lame shall not come into the house
cards.member_sentence: A saying from the siege of Zion that kept the blind and the lame out of the house, which Yahusha's (Jesus's) healing in the temple answers.
cards.flag: The old note called this a later categorical exclusion; the verses given do not show who made the saying a rule, so I wrote only that it could be turned into one.

cards.prose: In Isaiah's chapter Yahuah (the LORD) gives those with no standing a share inside his house: *a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters* (Isaiah 56:5). Matthew shows the blind and the lame coming to him in the temple and leaving whole. Isaiah's promise is to make them *joyful in my house of prayer*, and the house is where it happens.
cards.member_phrase: make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to make joyful in his house of prayer those he brings to his holy mountain.

cards.prose: The officials ask if he hears what the children are saying, and he answers out of the psalm. Matthew has *perfected praise* where the psalm says Yahuah (the LORD) has *ordained strength*, one line read for what it does: a child's praise is strength set against the enemy and the avenger. What was noise to the officials he reads as the psalm's own word.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings Yahuah (the LORD) has ordained strength against the enemy and the avenger.

cards.prose: The line he quotes belongs to the psalm that asks about *the son of Adam, that thou visitest him*. The children cry in the house, and the psalm sets beside them the son of Adam whom Elohim (God) visits, of whom the psalm says *crowned him with glory and honour* (Psalm 8:5). Son of Adam is the name Yahusha (Jesus) takes for himself in Matthew.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The psalm that gave him the babes' line goes on to ask why Elohim (God) visits the son of Adam.

cards.prose: He came to the tree hungry, and Matthew says what he found: *nothing thereon, but leaves only* (Matthew 21:19). Jeremiah had already used leaves without figs for a house about to lose what it was given. The verses before it say why, that the hurt of the daughter of my people had been healed slightly, *Peace, peace; when there is no peace* (Jeremiah 8:11).
cards.member_phrase: there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks of a house with no grapes, no figs, and a fading leaf, and of the things he gave passing away.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says he found Yashar'el (Israel) like *the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time*, and what came after was Baal-peor. Yahusha (Jesus) comes to a fig tree hungry for fruit, and the sentence on the tree is the old complaint, that what was firstripe turned to abomination. The judgment is on the fruitlessness, not on the existence of the people.
cards.member_phrase: I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baal-peor
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) saw the fathers like the firstripe figs, and then they went to Baal-peor.

cards.prose: Micah speaks as one who comes after the gathering and finds *no cluster to eat*, his soul longing for the firstripe fruit. Matthew's *he hungered* is the same longing, and the tree has only leaves. The verses after it say where the fruit went: *the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward* (Micah 7:3). The hunger is for a people's fruit, and the failure is in those set over them.
cards.member_phrase: there is no cluster to eat: my soul desired the firstripe fruit
cards.member_sentence: Micah comes after the gathering and finds no cluster to eat, though his soul desired the firstripe fruit.

cards.prose: Joel's fig tree is *barked* and made *clean bare*, and the chapter sets it beside a house that has lost its offering: *The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (Joel 1:9). Matthew sets a tree with no fruit beside the temple he has just cleared, and the two read together.
cards.member_phrase: He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast it away
cards.member_sentence: A vine laid waste and a fig tree stripped bare, in a land where the offering has been cut off from the house of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: The owner who goes looking for fruit and finds none is Isaiah's song before it is Matthew's fig tree. The beloved fenced and planted his vineyard, then *looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes* (Isaiah 5:2), and the song says whose vineyard it is: *the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 5:7). The tree with leaves and no fruit stands for that house.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's song of the beloved's vineyard begins on a very fruitful hill, the vineyard later found to bear wild grapes.

cards.prose: Twice he gives the disciples the mountain: once when they could not cast the devil out of the child, and he named *Because of your unbelief*, and again at the withered fig tree, where he says *doubt not*. It is the same saying both times, and what it asks for is faith without doubt.
cards.member_phrase: If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place
cards.member_sentence: Faith the size of a grain of mustard seed tells the mountain to move, and nothing is impossible to the one who says it.
cards.flag: I put the five faith and mountain cards in one new thread, since the fig tree thread is about fruitlessness and these are about faith and asking.

cards.prose: The mountains going into the sea is how the psalm pictures the worst that could happen, and the psalmist says *Therefore will not we fear*. The reason is the verse before it: *Elohim (God) is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble* (Psalm 46:1). The mountain Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to cast into the sea is the picture of what can be shaken, and faith that does not doubt rests on what cannot.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Even with the mountains carried into the sea the psalmist will not fear, because Elohim (God) is his refuge.

cards.prose: Isaiah says the mountains will depart and the hills be removed, and treats that as the movable part: what stays is *my kindness* and *the covenant of my peace*. When Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of a mountain cast into the sea, he speaks of what can move, and the faith he asks for leans on the word of Yahuah (the LORD) that does not.
cards.member_phrase: the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee
cards.member_sentence: Mountains and hills may be removed, but the kindness and the covenant of peace of Yahuah (the LORD) do not depart.

cards.prose: The promise that asking is answered is given its purpose here: whatever is asked in his name he will do *that the Father may be glorified in the Son*. Two verses later he says *If ye love me, keep my commandments* (John 14:15). So the answered prayer of Matthew is bound to the Father's glory and to the commandments, not to any wish.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: What is asked in his name he does, so that the Father is glorified in the Son.

cards.prose: In Matthew a word from him withers a tree and moves mountains, and a word of his made a man whole. He finds that man later in the temple and gives a second word, *sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee*. What he does by his word comes with a claim on how the man walks afterward.
cards.member_phrase: Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) finds the healed man in the temple and tells him to sin no more, lest something worse come.
cards.flag: The old note meant 1 John 5:14 ('according to his will'); the pair is John 5:14, so I wrote the card to the man made whole.

cards.prose: When they ask where his authority comes from, he sends them back to the wilderness of Judaea, where John came preaching. What John preached was *Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand* (Matthew 3:2), and Matthew says he was *spoken of by the prophet Isaiah* (Matthew 3:3). The question about authority is answered by who John was.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John the Baptist comes preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, the baptism Yahusha (Jesus) asks the priests about.

cards.prose: He once told the crowds that John was *more than a prophet*, the messenger of whom he said *Behold, I send my messenger before thy face* (Matthew 11:10). So when the priests cannot say whether John's baptism was from heaven or of men, they stand before a crowd that held John a prophet, and a question Yahusha (Jesus) had already answered in public.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells the crowds that John is a prophet and more than a prophet.

cards.prose: They ask *who gave thee this authority*, and Matthew has already shown who. A voice out of the cloud said *my beloved Son* and told the disciples *hear ye him*. It is the Father who speaks, giving his Son his place before them, and that is a credential no office in the temple could give.
cards.member_phrase: a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him
cards.member_sentence: A voice out of the cloud names Yahusha (Jesus) the beloved Son and tells the disciples to hear him.

cards.prose: The question about authority had its answer in Moses. A Prophet is raised up from among their brethren, like Moses, and *unto him ye shall hearken*. What marks him is not an office but what Yahuah (the LORD) puts in his mouth: *will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him* (Deuteronomy 18:18).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses says Yahuah (the LORD) will raise up a Prophet from among the brethren, like him, and the people are to hearken to him.

cards.prose: In the parable the father's word is *go work to day in my vineyard*, and in the Sermon the question is who does *the will of my Father which is in heaven*. The second son says yes and does not go, which is the *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)* kind of yes that gets no entry. It is the doing that is counted.
cards.member_phrase: he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Saying yes to the master is not enough to enter the kingdom; the one who does the will of the Father in heaven enters.

cards.prose: A son is known by whether he goes to the vineyard, not by being called a son. In Matthew 12 his own mother and brothers stand outside wanting to speak with him, and he stretches his hand toward his disciples and says *Behold my mother and my brethren!* (Matthew 12:49). Kin there is shown by who is with him, not by who stands outside.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: His mother and brothers stand outside wanting to speak with him, and he points to his disciples as his mother and brothers.
cards.flag: The pair is loose; the old note named only kinship being redefined, so I held to what the verses around it show.

cards.prose: The people of Ezekiel's day talked about the prophet at their walls and doors and told each other *Come, I pray you, and hear what is the word*. The lines after it say what that was worth: *they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness* (Ezekiel 33:31). That is the second son, yes in the mouth and no in the going.
cards.member_phrase: the children of thy people still are talking against thee by the walls and in the doors of the houses
cards.member_sentence: The people talk about the prophet at their doors and urge each other to hear the word, and the next lines show they will not do it.

cards.prose: The second son heard the order, said yes, and stayed where he was. James calls that man a hearer only, like one who looks in a mirror and goes off and forgets. The cure he gives is to be *doers of the word, and not hearers only*, and he ties it to looking into *the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein* (James 1:25).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: James says to be doers of the word and not hearers only, which is the difference between the two sons.

cards.prose: What counts at Cana, as in the vineyard, is the doing. His mother says only *They have no wine*, and then tells the servants *Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it* (John 2:5). The parable asks which son did what the father said, and the servants at the wedding are handed the same rule.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: At the wedding in Cana the mother of Yahusha (Jesus) brings him the need, then tells the servants to do whatever he says.
cards.flag: The old note meant 1 John 2:3 ('the 1234 of Truth'); the pair is John 2:3, so I wrote the card to Cana and the rule to do what he says.

cards.prose: The parable begins with Isaiah's song. The householder who planted, hedged and built a tower and winepress is the beloved who fenced and planted in Isaiah, and Isaiah says whose vineyard it is: *the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the men of Yahudah (Judah) his pleasant plant* (Isaiah 5:7). The husbandmen are the ones put in charge of it, not the vineyard.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's song of the beloved's vineyard, whose vineyard is named later as the house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: The vineyard in the parable is the vine the psalm says was brought out of Egypt and planted after the heathen were cast out. The psalm is a prayer for that vine, *Turn us again, O Elohim (God) of hosts, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved* (Psalm 80:7). In both the vine belongs to the one who planted it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) brought a vine out of Egypt, cast out the heathen, and planted it, the vine the parable's vineyard recalls.

cards.prose: The planter in the parable gives the vineyard everything, and Jeremiah has the planter's own voice saying what he planted: *a noble vine, wholly a right seed*. His question is how it became *the degenerate plant of a strange vine*. The charge in both is about what became of good planting.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) planted a noble vine, wholly a right seed, and asks how it turned into a strange degenerate plant.

cards.prose: Ezekiel's word of Yahuah (the LORD) about the vine asks what a vine tree is more than any tree of the forest and whether its wood is good for any work (Ezekiel 15:3). The answer is that *it is cast into the fire for fuel* (Ezekiel 15:4). The parable of the husbandmen is about a vineyard looked at for fruit, and a vine that gives none is judged for that, with the owner's care not in question.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel's word of Yahuah (the LORD) about the vine tree begins here and ends with the vine cast into the fire.

cards.prose: The mother in Ezekiel's lament is a vine planted by the waters, fruitful and full of branches, with *strong rods for the sceptres of them that bare rule* (Ezekiel 19:11). The same lament ends with *she was plucked up in fury, she was cast down to the ground* (Ezekiel 19:12). The vineyard in the parable begins as well planted as that, and the lament shows what its loss looks like.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: A mother vine planted by the waters, fruitful and full of branches, the picture of the vineyard before its loss.

cards.prose: The householder sends his servants for the fruit, and Yahuah (the LORD) says through Jeremiah that this is how it had been since Egypt: all his servants the prophets sent, *daily rising up early*. The beating and killing in the parable is the answer those servants got, and the answer is not new to this chapter.
cards.member_phrase: Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets
cards.member_sentence: From the day the fathers left Egypt, Yahuah (the LORD) sent all his servants the prophets, rising early to send them.

cards.prose: Twenty-three years of speaking and rising early, Jeremiah says, and *ye have not hearkened*. What the servants carried was an offer, *Turn ye again now every one from his evil way, and from the evil of your doings* (Jeremiah 25:5), and the husbandmen answer it with a beating, a killing and a stoning.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them; but ye have not hearkened
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sent all his servants the prophets, rising early to send them, and the people did not hearken.

cards.prose: *Stoned another* has a name behind it. Zechariah the son of Jehoiada was a priest on whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) came, and his words to the people were *Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)*. They *stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 24:21). A servant sent to hold the people to the commandments was killed at the house.
cards.member_phrase: Thus saith Elohim (God), Why transgress ye the commandments of Yahuah (LORD), that ye cannot prosper
cards.member_sentence: The Spirit of Elohim (God) comes on Zechariah the priest, who asks why the people transgress the commandments of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Urijah prophesied in the name of Yahuah (the LORD) against the city and the land, as Jeremiah did, and when King Jehoiakim and his princes heard his words the king sought to put him to death. Urijah fled to Egypt and was fetched back, and Jehoiakim *slew him with the sword, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people* (Jeremiah 26:23). So *killed another* in the parable has a name here.
cards.member_phrase: a man that prophesied in the name of Yahuah (LORD), Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kirjath-jearim
cards.member_sentence: Urijah prophesied in the name of Yahuah (the LORD) against the city and land, and the king later had him killed.

cards.prose: The servants in the parable are beaten and killed, and Jeremiah's own treatment was to be let down by cords into a dungeon with no water, where he sunk in the mire. The princes had said *We beseech thee, let this man be put to death* (Jeremiah 38:4), for the words he spoke to the people. The prophet was thrown in the pit for the words he was sent with.
cards.member_phrase: they let down Jeremiah with cords. And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire: so Jeremiah sunk in the mire
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah is lowered by cords into a dungeon with no water and sinks in the mire.

cards.prose: The prayer in Nehemiah tells it for the whole line: they *cast thy law behind their backs* and *slew thy prophets* who testified against them *to turn them to thee*. The servants in the parable come for fruit, and the prophets in the prayer came to turn the people back to the law, and they were killed for it.
cards.member_phrase: cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee
cards.member_sentence: They cast the law behind their backs and killed the prophets who testified against them to turn them back.

cards.prose: Elijah says at Horeb that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have *forsaken thy covenant* and *slain thy prophets with the sword*, and that he alone is left. The husbandmen who kill the servants are the same hands, and Elijah thinks he is the last servant standing. Yahuah (the LORD) had asked him *What doest thou here, Elijah?* (1 Kings 19:9).
cards.member_phrase: the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword
cards.member_sentence: Elijah says Yashar'el (Israel) has forsaken the covenant, thrown down the altars, and killed the prophets with the sword.

cards.prose: After the wind, the earthquake and the fire, a still small voice asks Elijah again what he is doing there, and he gives the same answer in the same words. The owner in the parable does not stop either: he goes on sending, as Yahuah (the LORD) answers Elijah's lament by sending him to anoint *Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room* (1 Kings 19:16).
cards.member_phrase: because the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword
cards.member_sentence: Elijah gives the same lament a second time, after the still small voice has asked him what he is doing there.

cards.prose: The husbandmen look at the heir and see only someone in the way. Isaiah's chapter of the servant begins by asking *Who hath believed our report?* and goes on to a servant who was *despised and rejected of men* (Isaiah 53:3), esteemed not. The parable lays that rejection in a vineyard.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's servant chapter opens by asking who has believed the report and to whom the arm of Yahuah (the LORD) is revealed.

cards.prose: The husbandmen say *among themselves*, *let us kill him*, and the psalm has the same scene: *the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:2). The plan is a *vain thing*, and the psalm does not end with the plot: *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh* (Psalm 2:4).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The heathen rage and the people imagine a vain thing, with rulers taking counsel against Yahuah (the LORD) and his anointed.

cards.prose: The heir is killed in the parable, and Daniel's verse names the one cut off, Messiah (Christ), in the words *Messiah be cut off, but not for himself*. It then says what follows, that the people of the prince that shall come *shall destroy the city and the sanctuary*. Daniel puts the cutting off first and the ruin of the city after it, and the owner in Matthew comes to the husbandmen after the heir is slain.
cards.member_phrase: And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself
cards.member_sentence: Daniel's verse says Messiah (Christ) is cut off, and that the city and the sanctuary are destroyed after it.
cards.flag: Held to what Daniel's verse itself says; nothing drawn from the weeks or from Revelation.

cards.prose: The husbandmen take the heir and the plan ends with him cast out. Hebrews says where Yahusha (Jesus) suffered, *without the gate*, and why, *that he might sanctify the people with his own blood*. It sets this beside the sin offering, whose bodies *are burned without the camp* (Hebrews 13:11).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) suffered outside the gate to sanctify the people with his own blood, as the sin offerings were burned outside the camp.

cards.prose: Stephen puts the parable into his own words to the council: *Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?* (Acts 7:52), and they slew those who spoke of the coming of the Just One, of whom the council were now the betrayers and murderers. He names a pattern in the rulers who sat before him, *as your fathers did, so do ye*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Stephen tells the council they always resist the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), as their fathers did before them.

cards.prose: He asks if they never read it, and the line he quotes comes from the psalm that gave the crowd its Hosanna earlier in this chapter. The one psalm holds both the welcome at the gate and the stone the builders refused, and what it says of the stone is that it is *marvellous in our eyes*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The stone the builders refused has become the head stone of the corner, a line from the same psalm the crowd sang at the entry.

cards.prose: Isaiah's stone is laid in Zion by Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) himself, tried and precious, a sure foundation, and the words just before it are spoken to *ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem* (Isaiah 28:14). That word to the rulers is what the stone is laid against, and it is set in Zion regardless.
cards.member_phrase: I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) himself lays in Zion a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation.

cards.prose: Isaiah says the same stone is a sanctuary to some and *a stone of stumbling* to *both the houses of Yashar'el (Israel)*. The builders who refuse it are not the only ones in view. It is a stone with two sides, a place to shelter and a place to fall.
cards.member_phrase: for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The stone is a sanctuary to some and a stone of stumbling to both houses of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) puts the word *stone* in front of the rulers, and Daniel has a stone too: *a stone was cut out without hands*, struck the image on its feet of iron and clay, and broke them to pieces. In Daniel *the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth* (Daniel 2:35), and the stone stands for a kingdom that breaks the kingdoms.
cards.member_phrase: a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces
cards.member_sentence: In Daniel a stone cut out without hands strikes the image on its feet of iron and clay and breaks it to pieces.

cards.prose: Daniel says what his stone is for: in the days of those kings the Elohim (God) of heaven sets up a kingdom that is never destroyed, and it breaks in pieces and consumes all the kingdoms. In Matthew the stone becomes *the head of the corner*, and in Daniel the same word becomes a kingdom that outlasts the ones it breaks.
cards.member_phrase: it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever
cards.member_sentence: The kingdom set up by the Elohim (God) of heaven is never destroyed, breaks in pieces all these kingdoms, and stands for ever.

cards.prose: Peter takes the line Yahusha (Jesus) used and says it to the rulers of his own day: the stone they *set at nought* is the one *whom ye crucified, whom Elohim (God) raised from the dead* (Acts 4:10). What the builders discarded, Elohim (God) raised.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Peter tells the rulers that the stone they set at nought has become the head of the corner.

cards.prose: Paul brings Isaiah's stone to answer why Yashar'el (Israel), *which followed after the law of righteousness* (Romans 9:31), did not reach it. He says they sought it not by faith, and stumbled at the stumblingstone. His complaint is with how they went after it, as if standing were a thing earned, and not with the law they were following.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul gives Isaiah's stone as the reason Yashar'el (Israel) stumbled, and says the one who believes on him will not be ashamed.

cards.prose: He says the builders refused the stone, and Paul says what house is being built: one on *the foundation of the apostles and prophets*, with Yahusha (Jesus) as the chief corner stone. The prophets are in the foundation first, so the stone is laid into what the prophets began and not on a new site.
cards.member_phrase: built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) himself being the chief corner stone
cards.member_sentence: The house is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Yahusha (Jesus) himself the chief corner stone.

cards.prose: Peter puts both halves of the psalm line in his own words. What the builders refused he calls *disallowed indeed of men*, and what became the head of the corner he calls *chosen of Elohim (God), and precious*. A few lines on he says it outright: *the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner* (1 Peter 2:7).
cards.member_phrase: as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of Elohim (God), and precious
cards.member_sentence: The living stone is disallowed by men and chosen by Elohim (God), and precious.

cards.prose: He has already said where the kingdom is headed: his followers on twelve thrones, *judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)*. Whatever nation is meant by the one that brings forth fruit, it is not a people outside those tribes, since the tribes are still the twelve he names.
cards.member_phrase: ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: Those who followed him sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), so the tribes are still twelve.

cards.prose: Peter uses the word the parable uses, *nation*, and says what it is: *an holy nation, a peculiar people*, and in the next lines *which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of Elohim (God)* (1 Peter 2:10). That is Hosea's not-my-people turned into my-people, so the nation that bears the fruit is Yashar'el (Israel) brought back and not another people set in its place.
cards.member_phrase: ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people
cards.member_sentence: Peter calls the people a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, and the next verse says they were once not a people.

cards.prose: The nation that is given the kingdom has a history that begins here, with a people told *ye are not my people*. Hosea names the loss, and a few lines on he names the repair: *in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God)* (Hosea 1:10). The keeping passes from husbandmen who failed it to the people who were Lo-ammi and are made Ammi.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) names the child Lo-ammi, not my people, the name Hosea's next verses promise to turn into sons of the living Elohim (God).

cards.prose: This is the reverse of Lo-ammi. The ones who were not his people are told they are, and they answer with their own confession, *Thou art my Elohim (God)*. The nation that brings forth fruit in Matthew is this people, sown back into the earth, with mercy on the one that had not obtained mercy.
cards.member_phrase: I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: The ones who were not his people are told You are my people, and they answer You are my Elohim (God).

cards.prose: The kingdom handed on to a nation is the second recovery. Yahuah (the Lord) reaches out a second time to bring back what is left of his people from Assyria, Egypt and the far places, and the verses after it say what that does to the old split: *The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Yahudah (Judah) shall be cut off* (Isaiah 11:13).
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) sets his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt and the far places.

cards.prose: The new covenant is made with two houses, *the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *the house of Yahudah (Judah)*, not with a third party. What is in it is the Torah: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* (Jeremiah 31:33). The kingdom given to a nation goes to the people who receive this covenant, and it puts the law in them, not away from them.
cards.member_phrase: I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah)
cards.member_sentence: The new covenant is made with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah), with the law written on their hearts.

cards.prose: A nation bringing forth fruit needs a heart that can, and Ezekiel says where it comes from. Yahuah (the LORD) takes away the stony heart and gives a heart of flesh, and the next verse says what that heart does: *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The fruit asked of the nation is walking in the Torah, and the new heart is how it is given.
cards.member_phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gives a new heart and a new spirit in place of the stony heart, and the next verse has it walking in his statutes.

cards.prose: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) that begins here is the two sticks, one for Yahudah (Judah) and one for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, joined into one in the prophet's hand. The verses after say what the one stick means: *I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 37:22). The nation in Matthew's verse is one nation, the two houses brought together, not a new people.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Here the word of Yahuah (the LORD) comes again to Ezekiel, introducing the two sticks that become one.

cards.prose: A nation that bears fruit needs a house to live in, and Paul describes one household of Elohim (God) built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets. The prophets are laid first, so the people he writes to stand on what the prophets spoke before the apostles did.
cards.member_phrase: built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) himself being the chief corner stone
cards.member_sentence: One household of Elohim (God) is built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Yahusha (Jesus) as the chief corner stone.
cards.flag: Ephesians 2:19's 'no more strangers and foreigners' is left unread either way; I wrote only the foundation, since the verses given do not settle who is meant.

cards.prose: A nation bringing forth fruit is named here by tribe. The sealed are an hundred and forty and four thousand *of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)*, and the verses that follow give the count tribe by tribe, beginning *Of the tribe of Judah were sealed twelve thousand* (Revelation 7:5). Revelation counts them by the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), by name.
cards.member_phrase: there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The sealed number an hundred and forty and four thousand, all of them from the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: The city has twelve gates with *the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* named on them, and its wall stands on *twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb* (Revelation 21:14). The nation the kingdom goes to is still twelve tribes in what Revelation shows, with the apostles in the foundations.
cards.member_phrase: had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The city's twelve gates carry the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: He asks the husbandmen for the fruits, and in the Sermon fruit is how he says anyone is known: *Ye shall know them by their fruits* (Matthew 7:16). The one who comes *in sheep's clothing* is not read by how he looks, and the nation the kingdom is given to is the one that bears. It is the same test in both places.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: False prophets come in sheep's clothing, and the Sermon says they are known by their fruits.

cards.prose: In John he names himself the true vine and says *my Father is the husbandman*, so the keeper of this vine is the Father himself and not the men in Matthew's parable who beat the servants. The Father's keeping is a husbandry of fruit: *Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit* (John 15:2).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) calls himself the true vine and says his Father is the husbandman.

cards.prose: James asks what profit there is in saying you have faith while you have no works, and answers a few lines on: *Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone* (James 2:17). The nation given the kingdom is the one that brings forth fruit, and James gives that fruit its name, works, which are judged *by the law of liberty* (James 2:12).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: James asks what it profits to say you have faith and have no works, and whether that faith can save.

cards.prose: Revelation closes on the same test: *Blessed are they that do his commandments*. The fruit the kingdom looks for from its nation is doing, and the verse sets the right to the tree of life and the way in through the gates of the city on the ones who do.
cards.member_phrase: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life
cards.member_sentence: Those who do his commandments are blessed and have the right to the tree of life and to enter the city by its gates.

cards.prose: *It will grind him to powder* is where Daniel's stone ends too. It strikes the image on its feet, and the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver and the gold *became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors* (Daniel 2:35), carried off by the wind. In Daniel the stone falls on kingdoms and breaks them, and in Matthew it falls on whoever stumbles against it.
cards.member_phrase: a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces
cards.member_sentence: Daniel's stone, cut out without hands, strikes the image and breaks it in pieces, so that the kingdoms are ground down.

cards.prose: *Whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken* is Isaiah's own order: the stone of stumbling, and then *many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken* (Isaiah 8:15). Isaiah says it is a stone of stumbling to both houses, so those who fall on it are of either house, and it is a sanctuary for the rest.
cards.member_phrase: for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The stone is a stumbling and a snare to both houses of Yashar'el (Israel), and many fall on it and are broken.

cards.prose: Isaiah's word is plain: *the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish*. The stone that grinds to powder whoever it falls on has this behind it. The verses around it are spoken to the city whose walls are built and whose gates stand open continually, and the line is the other side of that welcome: whatever will not serve her comes to nothing.
cards.member_phrase: the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted
cards.member_sentence: The nation and kingdom that will not serve Zion perishes and is utterly wasted.

cards.prose: At the end of the chapter *they perceived that he spake of them*, and later in Matthew they assemble at the high priest's palace and *consulted that they might take Yahusha (Jesus) by subtilty, and kill him* (Matthew 26:4). It is what the husbandmen said among themselves in the parable, and it is still said with an eye on the crowd: *Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar among the people* (Matthew 26:5).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The chief priests, scribes and elders gather at the palace of Caiaphas the high priest, where the plot against him is made.

cards.prose: Having perceived the parable was about them, the chief priests and Pharisees gather a council because of his miracles, and their talk is of keeping what they hold: *take away both our place and nation* (John 11:48). In the parable the husbandmen said *let us seize on his inheritance* (Matthew 21:38), and here the fear of losing a place is what they reason from.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The chief priests and Pharisees gather a council and ask what they will do, because the man does many miracles.

cards.prose: The chief priests and Pharisees *perceived that he spake of them*, and not every ruler closed the door: John says *among the chief rulers also many believed on him*. They kept quiet for fear of being put out, *For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of Elohim (God)* (John 12:43). The fear was a system's, and the rulers it held were not all of one mind.
cards.member_phrase: among the chief rulers also many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him
cards.member_sentence: Many of the chief rulers believed on him but did not confess him, for fear of being put out of the synagogue.

new_threads.title: By what authority: John's baptism and the voice from the cloud
new_threads.summary_md:
The chief priests and the elders come to him in the temple while he is teaching and put the question straight.

*By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?* (Matthew 21:23)

He does not dodge it. He asks them one in return, and the whole answer is folded into it.

*The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men?* (Matthew 21:25)

They cannot say heaven, because they would be asked why they did not believe him, and they will not say men, because they fear the people, who all hold John as a prophet. So the question about his authority is settled by what John was. Matthew had already told who John was, and Yahusha (Jesus) said he was more than a prophet.

*For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Isaiah, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of Yahuah (Lord), make his paths straight.* (Matthew 3:3)

Then there is the voice from the cloud, where the Father names his Son and tells the disciples to hear him.

*While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.* (Matthew 17:5)

None of this was new when it was said. Moses had told the people how a prophet would be known, and where he would come from.

*Yahuah Elohayka (The LORD thy God) will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken;* (Deuteronomy 18:15)

And he gave the credential itself, that Yahuah (the LORD) puts his words in the prophet's mouth.

*I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.* (Deuteronomy 18:18)

So the credential is not a title from the temple. It is John's baptism, which they would not own, and the Father's voice, and the Prophet Moses said would come from among his brethren. The question was asked by men who held the offices of the house, and the answer was written in the book they read.

new_threads.title: Faith that does not doubt, and the mountain cast into the sea
new_threads.summary_md:
After the fig tree withers the disciples marvel, and he turns the wonder into a saying about faith.

*Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.* (Matthew 21:21)

He had said the same about a mountain before, when the disciples could not cast the devil out of a child and he named their unbelief.

*If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.* (Matthew 17:20)

The mountains were already a way of speaking in the psalms and the prophets, and they were never the steady thing. The psalmist says the mountains may go into the sea and he will not fear, because Elohim (God) is his refuge.

*Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;* (Psalm 46:2)

Isaiah says it from the other side. Mountains go, and what Yahuah (the LORD) has covenanted does not.

*For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith Yahuah (LORD) that hath mercy on thee.* (Isaiah 54:10)

So faith that tells a mountain to be removed is leaning on the one who does not move. John gives the same promise a purpose, and a line about the commandments follows close behind it.

*And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.* (John 14:13)

*If ye love me, keep my commandments.* (John 14:15)

And when a man made whole is found in the temple, the healing is followed by a charge.

*Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.* (John 5:14)

Faith, asking, and what he does with the asking run in one line. The power is the Father's, the asking is in the Son's name, and what is given is given to someone who is then to walk straight.
